key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow by slowing early deformation, with Cr-enriched and Ni-depleted boundaries strengthening the alloy response.
engineering_relevance: Targeting grain-boundary chemistry offers a practical route to improve high-temperature strength and delay yielding in nanocrystalline stainless steels.
method: Hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Comparison against annealed and random controls on the same microstructures
Constant-stress and fixed-strain-rate mechanical tests across multiple temperatures
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random ones, and showed a 6-7% higher peak stress than annealed controls at 300, 750, and 950 K.
watch_item: The measured segregation strength depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so composition metrics must be interpreted carefully when comparing studies.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
